The initial cost of planting the tree is $90.  
Each year, the tree produces 7 lemons, which are sold for $1.50 each, giving a yearly income of \(7 \times 1.5 = \$10.50\).  
The yearly maintenance cost is $3, so the net profit per year is \(10.50 - 3 = \$7.50\).

To find how many years it takes to recover the $90 cost and start earning money, divide the initial cost by the yearly profit:  
\(90 \div 7.5 = 12\) years to break even.  

After 12 years, the total profit exactly equals the cost ($90), so no money has been earned yet. In the 13th year, the cumulative profit becomes $97.50, meaning Carlos starts earning money.

Answer: 13

He starts earning money once the cumulative profit exceeds the initial cost.
Let t be the number of years.
Cumulative profit = 7.5 * t.
We need 7.5 * t > 90.
t > 90 / 7.5 = 12.
So t must be > 12. Since t is integer years, after 12 years cumulative profit is exactly 90, so he breaks even. He starts earning money after that, i.e., in the 13th year. But the question asks: "How many years will it take before he starts earning money on the lemon tree?" This usually means the number of full years until the cumulative net profit is positive. After 12 years, net is 0, not yet earning money. After 13 years, net is +7.5, so he starts earning money. So answer: 13 years.
